A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same cluster-based watermarking research for autoregressive image generators. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison despite the ClusterMark renaming and substantial revision.

before.justification: Section 4 and the appendices report original watermark-detection, image-quality, runtime and ablation results for LlamaGen GPT-B, GPT-L and RAR-XL.

after.justification: Original experiments remain and are extended with token-classifier comparisons, additional baselines, CLIP scores, geometric-transformation tests and cluster-initialization analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 adds a token classifier trained with token-label cross-entropy, whose predictions can subsequently be mapped to clusters. V1 trained only a direct cluster classifier. This extends the reconstruction component while retaining the core k-means clustering, green-set construction and biased sampling procedure.

E1.justification: The ImageNet class-conditioned image coverage remains unchanged, but v2 adds a substantial family of geometric test scenarios: translation, cropping, flipping, perspective, rotation, scaling and combined scaling/blur (Tables 8–10). V1 discussed geometric vulnerability without reporting these evaluations.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds TrustMark and SSL for all three models and WMAR (FT+AUGS) for RAR-XL, while removing DWT-DCT. IndexMark (+IE), DWT-DCT-SVD and RivaGAN remain in the main comparison. Appendix Table 7 separately removes all its post-hoc comparator rows, including DWT-DCT-SVD and RivaGAN.

E3.justification: Figure 3 switches from weak perturbation Set A to stronger Set B. Figure 5 changes the model, prefixes, green fraction and perturbations used for the prefix analysis. New protocols include CLIP evaluation on 50,000 images and inverse-transformation/SyncSeal controls. TrustMark uses its built-in detection procedure rather than the empirical ROC procedure used for other methods.

E4.justification: V2 adds token-classifier comparisons with and without clustering, geometric failure and recovery controls, sensitivity to cluster initialization, and CLIP-based analysis of semantic fidelity. The revised prefix case study includes an image and token-pattern example to investigate false positives. These substantially extend v1's cluster-count, watermark-strength, green-fraction and prefix ablations.

E5.justification: V2 reports variation across six cluster initializations in Table 6 and newly discloses consistent generation seeds across experiments. Eight-prefix averages and standard-deviation bands already existed in v1 and remain for training-free plots. However, v1's detailed Tables 8–9 of prefix-wise AUC/TPR means and standard deviations, including cluster-classifier variability, are removed.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive classifier, baseline, geometric, CLIP and runtime results and revises multiple Table 1 estimates. For example, RAR-XL's training-free 64-cluster blur TPR is 0.163 in v1 and 0.100 in v2; the revised test-sample documentation prevents treating this as an established controlled performance decline. Own-method Set A values in Table 7 remain unchanged, while its baseline rows and the old prefix-summary tables disappear.

T1.justification: Section 2.2 corrects the formal rejection condition from rejecting when the p-value exceeds the threshold to rejecting when it is below the threshold, explicitly identifying the right-tailed probability. V1's algorithm already computed a right-tailed p-value, so this establishes a correction to the stated mathematics rather than an implemented detector change. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the novelty statement from AR watermarking being unexplored to underexplored. The contributions and conclusion now include token prediction alongside cluster prediction and explicitly claim superiority to concurrent AR methods, including WMAR. The central claim that clustering improves robustness while preserving image quality remains.

C2.justification: V2 attributes unfavorable-prefix false positives to repetitive token transitions in uniform image regions. It develops v1's geometric limitation into an explanation involving spatial synchronization and recoverability. New Appendix D introduces private-model/API deployment assumptions and discusses prefix-search security and larger key spaces, substantially expanding applicability boundaries and security qualifications.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a ClusterMark source-code link instead of v1's future-release promise. Appendices A–B clarify tuning/test sample separation and image reuse, add baseline implementation details such as TrustMark configuration Q, and specify the CLIP text template. These are documentation and access-information additions; they do not establish that previously unspecified settings changed. The existing classifier training budget remains.

R1.justification: V2 adds references and context for TrustMark, SSL, SyncSeal, CLIPScore, BitMark, Safe-VAR and watermark attacks. Section 5 refines comparisons with IndexMark and WMAR, including the distinction concerning decoder fine-tuning. WMAR was already discussed in v1; its new experimental participation is separate from these positioning changes.

P1.justification: V2 extensively revises prose across the abstract, method explanation, evaluation discussion and conclusion, adopts ClusterMark/KGW terminology, and reorganizes the experimental setup and appendix explanations. The title, author information and acknowledgements also change. The broad main-section order remains, but the editorial revision extends well beyond isolated corrections.

P2.justification: The pipeline diagram is redrawn, the prefix figure gains image/token illustrations, and a main-text sample montage is introduced. Main comparison tables expand, runtime presentation changes to milliseconds, and perturbation-setting tables are merged. New CLIP and robustness displays accompany removal of the old prefix-summary tables and substantial appendix reformatting; retained sample galleries are largely relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the evidence by comparing against WMAR and additional post-hoc methods, isolating clustering's contribution with a trained-token control, and testing the geometric failure conditions that v1 only discussed. Clearer tuning/test documentation and code-access information further improve assessability. These gains outweigh the loss of detailed prefix statistics and some overgeneralized summaries: notably, the claimed 99+% SyncSeal recovery has a 95.1% GPT-L scaling result in Table 10.
